newsitem.title: USA: U.S. should cut off aid to Palestinians - Gingrich.
newsitem.headline: U.S. should cut off aid to Palestinians - Gingrich.

text.p: House Speaker Newt Gingrich said on Friday that U.S. aid to the Palestinian Authority should be cut off unless the authority takes a tougher stand against bomb attacks on Israeli civilians.

"I favour insisting that the Palestinian authority take serious steps against terrorism or they are not to get help," Gingrich said on his first stop home after the August recess. The Georgia Republican was speaking to reporters after a speech in his suburban Atlanta district.
A double suicide attack on Wednesday ravaged Jerusalem's main Jewish market and killed 13 people.

The House quickly adopted an amendment to the fiscal 1998 appropriations bill to suspend up to $20 million in aid for administration to the Palestinian Authority, part of a $100 million pledge for 1998.
The United States has pledged $500 million over five years to the authority, about $220 million of which has already been sent.

"Frankly, I think the Palestinian authority has a great deal to answer for, and I think if there is not some very significant effort on their part to stop terrorism, there is a very high likelihood the United States will cease to give aid to the Palestinian authority," Gingrich said.
He charged that "the chief of police of Palestine has been actively supporting the terrorists."
